title: Incident-driven test coverage for intermittent routing + KV-cache drift
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: A customer-facing spike in generation-quality failures was observed across multiple hosted endpoints between 2025-02-15 and 2025-02-17. Automatic eval alerts showed a 6-8% drop on the 'policy-guidance' prompt set. Root-cause analysis indicates a correlated interaction between routing fallbacks (when the primary model variant was temporarily unavailable) and a KV cache TTL propagation bug that allowed stale KV entries to be reused across model-variant boundaries. This ticket bundles the follow-up work: define targeted evals that reproduce the routing+cache interaction, implement new synthetic test cases, add a deterministic replay harness for the failing sessions, and extend monitoring/playbook so future incidents are caught and mitigated faster.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Repro test that triggers the same quality delta deterministically in CI (pass/fail), covering routing fallback + stale-KV scenario
A2: New eval cohort (routing-cache-interaction) added to daily regression pipeline with a clear alerting threshold and dashboard
A3: Playbook updated with rollback steps and a triage checklist for routing-related quality dips
A4: One mitigation implemented (either TTL fix or routing policy guard) with a canary rollout and metrics showing regression eliminated on canary traffic
tasks: T1: Capture sample failing sessions from logs and export to replay bundle (assigned: Arjun)
T2: Design a small synthetic prompt set that exercises long-prefix KV caching and model-variant switching (assigned: Maya)
T3: Implement a deterministic replay harness for the bundle that can run in the eval pipeline (assigned: Eng QA)
T4: Add regression job to daily evals pipeline and add Grafana dashboard panels for the new cohort (assigned: Observability)
T5: Patch KV TTL propagation so entries are namespaced by model-variant; add unit + integration tests (assigned: Runtime)
T6: Update routing policy to prefer same-variant affinity for sessions < 2 minutes; run canary (assigned: Serving)
T7: Draft and publish incident handoff / playbook in Confluence and link to ticket (assigned: Maya)
T8: Postmortem note and customer email template drafted for Success (assigned: Maya)
comments: 2025-02-18 - Maya Chen: Initial triage complete; observed correlation between model fallback events (region us-west-2) and eval delta on 'policy-guidance' set. Exported 42 sample sessions to /artifacts/replay-bundles/routing-kv-20250217.tar.gz. Next: reproduce locally.

2025-02-19 - Arjun Patil: Reproduced deterministic failure in local replay harness when injecting a routing fallback at token 12 and forcing KV TTL to a higher epoch. Filed a small repro PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4356 (WIP).

2025-02-20 - Runtime team (notes): root cause hypothesis: KV keys weren't namespaced by model-variant checksum during TTL refresh which allowed variant A's KV entries to be used after fallback to variant B. Also discovered routing affinity window default is 0s in config which increases fallback frequency for short sessions.

2025-02-21 - Observability: added eval cohort 'routing-cache-interaction' to daily jobs; initial nightly run shows the cohort failing in 4/10 runs with the existing runtime. Grafana panel added: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/quality/routing-cache-interaction

2025-02-21 - Maya Chen: Plan of record: (1) land namespacing patch + tests, (2) add minimal routing affinity guard for short sessions behind feature flag, (3) add replay job to CI, (4) ship playbook. Prioritizing namespacing patch for canary later this week.
